name: Opposite Sections of a Degree-Two Corner Obey a Sharp Support Bound
statement: Let $A,B,C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ contain zero, with $n\le7$, and suppose $Y=\{(0,00)\}\cup(A\times\{01\})\cup(B\times\{10\})\cup(C\times\{11\})$ is ample. Put $K=A\cap C$, $\mathcal G=\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(K)$, and let $\mathcal L$ be the supports containing no member of $\mathcal G$. Then $|B\setminus C|\le|\mathcal L\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(A)|$. If $(0,00)$ is the unique corner of $Y$, the right side is at least nine. The same conclusions hold after exchanging $A$ and $B$.
proof: Ample section-reduction identities give $\operatorname{Sh}(A\cap C)=\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ and the analogous identity for $B\cap C$. The four-section criterion gives $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{Sh}(C)$, so the down-set $\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ avoids every member of $\mathcal G$ and lies in $\mathcal L$. Its part outside $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ injects into $\mathcal L\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(A)$ and has cardinality $|B\setminus C|$. If that bound were at most eight, a nonempty $B\setminus C$ would have a relative corner outside $C$; if $B\subseteq C$ and $|B|>1$, a prescribed-endpoint peeling supplies a nonzero corner; and if $B=\{0\}$, its displayed square vertex is a corner. Each case gives a second corner of $Y$, proving the lower bound nine under uniqueness.
